name: Paisalo Digital Ltd
title: Paisalo Digital Ltd - 532900 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Paisalo grew AUM 33% and PAT 27% in Q2 with NIM at 5.7% vs ~6% target, cost of funds down to 10%, and management leaning on yield-timing and AI-efficiency explanations; no capacity or industry supply discipline evidence.

triggers.label: Drought pockets tighten underwriting

we are definitely expecting the NIMs to close at about 6%.

guidance.value: live in Q3, metrics from Q1 FY28

we'll target somewhere around the 15% to 18% range on a sustained annualized basis

summary.headline: Paisalo Q2 FY27 PAT up 27% YoY to INR656 million; AUM up 33% to INR72,659 million with gross NPA at 0.66%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed strong growth in AUM, disbursements and profit, with asset quality improving year-on-year. Disbursements rose 42% YoY to INR15,673 million in the quarter, and credit cost fell to 0.4% from 1.1%. Reported yields and NIM were diluted by late-quarter fund deployment, which management says is transient. Management flagged drought-related pressure in parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and tightened underwriting and moderated rural disbursements there.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA down 15 bps YoY, NNPA down 19 bps YoY
Cost of borrowing 10%, down ~50 bps YoY

segments.name: Distribution footprint
segments.commentary: 6,415 touchpoints across 23 states: 426 branches, 4,299 distribution points and 1,690 business correspondent touchpoints. Customer base about 20 million.

segments.name: Business correspondent network
segments.commentary: 1,690 touchpoints served about 1.93 million customers; partners are SBI, Bank of India and Indian Overseas Bank.

segments.name: Agri and allied portfolio
segments.commentary: Agri and allied make up about 15% of the portfolio; the balance spans food and hospitality, street vendors, healthcare, education, MSME, transport and others.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 cost of funds guidance of about 10.5%; current cost of funds at 10%, with management expecting a 25-30 bps rise from the RBI rate hike, already priced in.
NIM expected to close FY27 at about 6% annualised versus 5.7% currently.
App go-live targeted by end of Q3 FY27, with metrics shared from Q1 FY28; app-led acquisition expected at 40-50% of acquisition within three years.
Management targets doubling AUM, revenue and PAT over the next three fiscal years; operating leverage gains expected around Q1 FY28 onwards.
Long-term targets: ROE 15-18% sustained; ROA 4-4.5% (currently about 3.3-3.4%).
capex_capacity: Branch-led footprint with asset-light distribution expansion via distribution points and business correspondents; touchpoints have roughly doubled each year.
25 live AI bots; AI onboarding processed about 1.90 lakh applications in Q2 and outbound calling about 3 lakh calls daily.
Employee headcount down 11% YoY despite 33% AUM growth (about 3% reduction in Q1, per management).
Public NCD issuance raised about INR294.9 crore under INR900 crore shelf; INR124.47 crore unsecured private placement in September; over INR177 crore raised via commercial paper in H1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Southwest monsoon ended at about 87% of long period average; kharif sowing down about 1% YoY and at 101% of normal acreage.
Maharashtra most affected; parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana have patchy rainfall; some districts declared drought-affected. Rural disbursements moderated in those districts.
Management says yields were diluted only transiently by late-quarter deployment of borrowed funds; no yield cut made to enter geographies or products.
Early October business momentum described as encouraging; rural and semi-urban vehicle registrations growing slightly faster than urban in H1.
Co-lending with SBI remains at status quo; company is compliant and waiting for banks to complete their CIF and CBS set-up.

qa_highlights.question: How will the RBI rate hike affect lending and borrowing yields and NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a 25-30 bps rise in cost of funds, already priced in; cost of funds is at 10% against a 10.5% full-year guidance. NIM is expected to close near 6% versus 5.7% now.

qa_highlights.question: Is yield moderation timing or mix or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly timing: most disbursements came late in Q2, creating a denominator effect. Management says yields will normalise in Q3 and Q4 with no deliberate yield cut.

qa_highlights.question: Will headcount reduction and AI-led efficiency continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount fell 11% YoY versus 33% AUM growth. Management expects this to normalise into festive season and Q4 as operating leverage matures, with the app and AI framework adding a further step-up from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: When will AI and digital initiatives show up in cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the impact comes around Q1 FY28 onwards, with a clearer downward trend in operating leverage towards the end of the three-year cycle; maker-checker controls keep AI from running operations alone.

qa_highlights.question: Why is finance cost growth (about 33%) ahead of income growth (about 24%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to late deployment of recently raised public and unsecured NCD funds, which sat as treasury surplus at quarter end; management expects this to normalise in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term ROE and ROA aspirations and what is the consumer app timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: ROE target 15-18% and ROA 4-4.5%. App targeted to go live by end of Q3, with metrics from Q1 FY28; app-led acquisition expected at 40-50% over three years.

risks_watch: Drought-related stress in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; kharif outcome to be clear by end October or early November; agri half-yearly repayments make early read on portfolio performance uncertain.
Rate hike cycle: RBI not expected to cut for a couple of quarters; management expects 25-30 bps cost of funds rise.
Yield and NIM recovery depends on the Q3-Q4 normalisation of late-quarter deployment; NIM must move from 5.7% toward about 6%.
Execution on app launch (Q3 target) and AI framework; headcount falling 11% while the AI maker-checker framework is still in place.
Co-lending volume with SBI and other banks is on hold until partner banks complete their technical compliance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and funding, while cautious on the rural and drought-affected book. Management was defensive on the Q2 yield dip and the 33% finance cost rise versus 24% income growth, attributing both to transient late-quarter deployment.
key_quotes: So we definitely expect that there is going to be about a 25 to 30 basis point increase, which we have already priced in.
Despite 33% year-on-year growth in AUM and continued expansion of our network, our employee base declined by 11% year-on-year during the quarter.
So this is just a temporary transient impact on a short-term basis.
